subject: general
question: What is India’s renewable energy target by the year 2030 in terms of installed capacity?
solution:
The correct answer is __**500 GW**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• India has set an ambitious target of achieving **500 GW of renewable energy installed capacity** by the year 2030.
 
• This target includes contributions from various renewable sources such as **solar, wind, hydropower, and biomass.**
 
• The initiative is part of India's commitment under the **Paris Agreement** to combat climate change and reduce carbon emissions.
 
• India aims to fulfill **50% of its energy requirements** from renewable sources by 2030.
 
• As of 2023, India has already achieved around **125 GW of renewable energy capacity**, showcasing significant progress toward the 2030 goal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Solar Mission (NSM):**

 
 
• Launched in 2010, NSM is part of India's National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC).
 
• It aims to establish India as a global leader in solar energy by achieving a target of **100 GW of solar capacity** by 2022.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement:**
 
 
• An international treaty adopted in 2015 to combat climate change.
 
• India pledged to reduce its carbon intensity by **33-35% by 2030** compared to 2005 levels.
 
• Renewable energy targets are a key component of India's commitment under this agreement.
 
 
 
• **International Solar Alliance (ISA):**
 
 
• Founded by India and France in 2015, ISA is a treaty-based intergovernmental organization.
 
• Its objective is to promote the use of solar energy globally and mobilize financial resources for its expansion.
 
 
 
• **Green Energy Corridor Project:**
 
 
• A government initiative to integrate renewable energy into India's power grid.
 
• The project involves setting up transmission networks to handle renewable energy efficiently.
